significance: A Vishnu temple at Denkanikottai in the Tamil Nadu-Karnataka border country, built in the Hoysala idiom with a five-tiered rajagopuram; the Wodeyars of Mysore endowed its major shrines and pillared halls in the 16th century.
story: The Skanda Purana account here has Venkateswara appearing to the sage Kanva to save him from the yaksha Devandagadagan, taking the form of a hunter and killing the yaksha with a mace called Denkani, from which the town takes its name.
